verdicts.quote: "Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints." ([developer.woocommerce.com](https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/apis/rest-api/authentication/))
verdicts.reason: WooCommerce issues per‑store REST API keys (consumer key/secret) that clients use to authenticate; this is an API key model, even though they’re sent via Basic Auth over HTTPS.

verdicts.quote: "To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API." ([developer.woocommerce.com](https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/apis/rest-api/authentication/))
verdicts.reason: Store admins can generate their own keys in the dashboard; no paid tier or review is required for core REST API access.

verdicts.quote: "The coupons API allows you to create, view, update, and delete..." plus sections for Customers, Orders, Products, Taxes, Settings, Shipping, Webhooks, Reports, etc. ([developer.woocommerce.com](https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/apis/rest-api/v3/))
verdicts.reason: The v3 reference lists dozens of resources across the product and supports full CRUD for core objects, indicating broad coverage.

verdicts.quote: "Connect an external Model Context Protocol (MCP) client to your store’s WooCommerce AI server." ([woocommerce.com](https://woocommerce.com/document/woocommerce-ai/mcp-server/?utm_source=openai))
verdicts.reason: WooCommerce’s own docs describe an official MCP server for stores (with WordPress.com OAuth) and an optional direct API‑key transport.

verdicts.quote: "To start using REST API, you first need to generate API keys." ([developer.woocommerce.com](https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/apis/rest-api/))
verdicts.reason: Keys are self‑serve and the REST API is documented with straightforward auth and CRUD endpoints, so Composio could ship an integration today without special approvals.
